Chapter 5 of 5 // Athletic Rivalries Archive

Blood Feuds of the Commonwealth

VPU (1989) //, #6 Monongahela State (2004) //, Virginia Dominion (2014–2015)

1. The Three Pillars of Forger Rivalry Lore

In the RaggieSoft universe, every autumn Saturday in Blacksburg is measured against three opponent institutions—each representing a distinct cultural, geographic, and historical clash with Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI):

THE OLD GUARD EST. 1895

Virginia Piedmont Univ. (VPU)

Charlottesville, VA // The Commonwealth Cup

Blue-collar Appalachian engineering versus Charlottesville patrician tradition. During a freezing November 1989 clash against VPU, students stomping heavy winter boots on The Anvil's steel bleachers birthed "The Stomp" and the deafening "IGNITION!" crowd chant.

BORDER WAR BLACK ANVIL

Monongahela State (MSU)

Morgantown, WV // The Coalminers

"The Coal & Iron War." A bruising Appalachian border blood feud. On Saturday, October 8, 2004, CPI upset #6 MSU (19–13) on the night "Saturday Night Lights: The Crucible" secretly premiered at the start of the 4th quarter.

THE BLOOD FEUD 2014 – 2015

Virginia Dominion (VDU)

Norfolk, VA // The Monarchs ("Norfolk")

"The Hammer vs. The Crown." Back-to-back Homecoming shutouts in 2014 (38–0 VDU) and 2015 (52–0 CPI) turned the upstart Monarchs from Hampton Roads into a personal blood feud that eclipsed the century-old VPU series.

2. The Hammer vs. The Crown: The 2014–2015 VDU Homecoming Shutout War

2014 – 2015 ARCHIVE

How back-to-back Homecoming shutouts turned Virginia Dominion University ("Norfolk") into the most combustible rivalry in Commonwealth sports history.

For decades, every CPI student and alumnus considered Virginia Piedmont University (VPU) to be the Forgers' undisputed arch-rival. That changed forever across twelve months in 2014 and 2015, when CPI scheduled a home-and-home non-conference series against Virginia Dominion University (VDU)—the upstart Monarchs out of Norfolk, Virginia. Because both schools weaponized their respective Homecoming Saturdays to stage the matchups—and both games ended in shocking, lopsided shutouts—the collision between the Blue Ridge Mountains ("Blacksburg") and Hampton Roads ("Norfolk") became an unforgettable chapter in CPI lore.

Act I: "The Homecoming Humiliation" SEPT 27, 2014
VISITOR (UNRANKED)
VDU Monarchs
38
HOME (#3 IN NATION — CPI HOMECOMING)
CPI Forgers
0

The Hubris: On Saturday, September 27, 2014, CPI hosted VDU inside The Crucible for the very first time. Ranked #3 in the nation with a Gridiron Trophy-candidate quarterback, CPI Athletics had scheduled unranked VDU as what everyone assumed would be effortless Homecoming "target practice." All week long, dorm doors across Bennett Hall and chalk murals on The Commonwealth Green depicted the CPI Forger's Hammer smashing the VDU Monarch's Crown under banners reading "BEAT NORFOLK!"

The Collapse: After CPI marched down the field on the opening drive only to push a chip-shot field goal wide left, VDU's unflashy, brute-force rushing attack systematically ground down the #3 Forgers. Eating the clock 4 and 5 yards at a time, VDU stunned the 65,000-strong crowd to lead 7–0 after the first quarter and 24–0 at halftime (after recovering a CPI fumble inside the final minute of the half). Thousands of stunned fans streamed for the exits as the Marching Forgers took the field, and VDU poured it on in the second half to seal a historic 38–0 shutout inside The Crucible.

Act II: "The Norfolk Reckoning" OCT 2015
VISITOR (THE RECEIPTS)
CPI Forgers
52
HOME (VDU HOMECOMING — NORFOLK, VA)
VDU Monarchs
0

The Arrogance: Intoxicated by their 2014 upset in Blacksburg, VDU's administration made the fateful decision to schedule the 2015 return leg in Norfolk as VDU's own Homecoming Game. Student groups in Norfolk printed thousands of commemorative "38–0" t-shirts, convinced they would humiliate CPI a second time in front of their own alumni.

The Receipts: CPI's players and coaching staff had spent 365 days staring at the 0–38 scoreboard stenciled onto every weight-room mirror in Blacksburg. Refusing to take their foot off the gas for sixty minutes, the Forgers walked into VDU's Homecoming party in Norfolk and delivered a merciless, retaliatory 52–0 shutout blowout—refusing to kick field goals, keeping their starting defense on the field until the final whistle to preserve the goose egg, and handing VDU an even larger Homecoming shutout humiliation on their own turf.

Cross-Universe Narrative Connection: The Aubrie Chronicles & Reclaiming The Crucible (2016)

In RaggieSoft's literary canon (The Aubrie Chronicles), the September 27, 2014 Homecoming Humiliation (38–0) was the traumatic freshman-year game where Jordan Shawn Kelly—watching his new Blacksburg sanctuary get dismantled by the team from his abusive mother's Hampton Roads backyard—suffered a devastating halftime meltdown and fled back to Bennett Hall Suite 214 with the Group of 8. Jordan did not set foot inside The Crucible again for nearly two years—until Saturday, May 21, 2016, when The Stardust Engine returned home to Blacksburg to film and record Live at the Crucible, overwriting the ghost of the 38–0 scoreboard beneath a tidal wave of 65,000 fans singing "Electric Color" in unison.
